evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Never asked. Rep jumps directly into confirming logistics details.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No concerns probed at step 2. Customer's cost concern emerged naturally at step 5 ('I was hoping to get closer to $1,000') but rep did not dig two layers deep into it.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Rep mentions Sunday is $20/hour cheaper than Saturday ('the rate for Sunday is cheaper compared to Saturday like $20 difference per hour') but frames the saving as an hourly difference, not a total dollar amount. No explicit flexibility ask. Quote: 'And another gate use is the rate for Sunday is cheaper compared to Saturday like $20 difference per hour.'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: No rate lock or no-deposit guarantee mentioned. Rep says 'if you're ready to proceed, then you can just give us a callback' — which is a built-in out. No plain ask for the business. Quote: 'So, yeah. But you know, I'll go ahead and send you an email for this estimate, and if you're ready to proceed, then you can just give us a callback.'

top_strength: Rep gathered substantial logistics detail (home size, bedroom count, furniture inventory, special items, distance, box estimates) and delivered two personalized estimates (6–7 hours at $1,276–$1,670, then refined to 5–6 hours at $1,050–$1,260) anchored to the customer's specific move profile.
coaching_note: You skipped the two-concerns question entirely, never delivered the On-Time Guarantee or No Worries Damage Coverage promises, did not ask for the business directly, and framed the Value Days saving as an hourly difference instead of a total dollar amount — each of these is a core v4 behavior that must land on every call.
